material.name: refractory metal high entropy alloy
material.initial_state: mixture of easily available elemental powders

intervention.description: in-situ alloy formation from mixtures of elemental powders

structure.description: complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles

evidence_units.mechanism: favorable process parameter combinations enable complete fusion and in-situ alloy formation
evidence_spans: For this reason, the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work.
In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed to avoid an expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder.

It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.
The relative density of the samples with a dimension of 6 × 6 × 6 mm 3 reaches, in dependence of the PBF-LB/M parameter set, 99.8%.
Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) measurements confirm the presence of a single bcc-phase.
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show a dendritic and/or cellular microstructure that can, to some extent, be controlled by the PBF-LB/M parameters.
limitations: microstructure control is only to some extent achievable

material.name: WMoTaNbV
material.composition: W20 Mo20 Ta20 Nb20 V20 (atomic percent)
material.initial_state: heterogeneous mixture of five single element powders

intervention.description: The amount of Vanadium in the initial powder mixture was increased by a factor of 1.5 compared to the other alloying elements to pre-compensate the expected evaporation of V during PBF-LB/M.

parameters.powder_drying: dried in a vacuum furnace at 120 °C for 8 h
parameters.powder_mixing: mixed for 1 h in a Turbular-mix

structure.description: powder blend with spherical particles for W, Mo, Ta, Nb and irregular shaped milled particles for V

evidence_units.mechanism: To pre-compensate for the common phenomenon of selective evaporation of lower boiling alloying elements during PBF-LB/M, specifically targeting Vanadium which has the lowest boiling point in the WMoNbTaV system.

outcome.property: intentional adjustment of initial V content

comparison.baseline_material: standard W20 Mo20 Ta20 Nb20 V20 alloy composition

evidence_spans: Since selective evaporation of lower boiling alloying elements is a common phenomenon in PBF-LB/M [ [41] ], the amount of Vanadium, which has the lowest boiling point in the WMoNbTaV system [ [26] ], in the initial powder mixture was increased by a factor of 1.5 compared to the other alloying elements to pre-compensate the expected evaporation of V during PBF-LB/M.

material.name: WMoTaNbV
material.composition: W20 Mo20 Ta20 Nb20 V20 (atomic percent)
material.initial_state: powders with D90 of 23.1 µm for W, 36.1 µm for Ta, and other particles

intervention.description: A smaller D90 was chosen for W and Ta to ease fusion during PBF-LB/M and avoid undissolved particles.

structure.description: powder blend with predominantly spherical particles except for V

evidence_units.mechanism: To facilitate fusion during PBF-LB/M and avoid undissolved particles by reducing particle size for high-melting elements.
evidence_spans: For the high-melting elements W and Ta a smaller D 90 (23.1 µm and 36.1 µm respectively) was chosen to ease fusion during PBF-LB/M and to avoid undissolved particles.

material.name: WMoTaNbV
material.composition: W20 Mo20 Ta20 Nb20 V20 (atomic percent)

intervention.action: PBF-LB/M processing with specific parameter set
intervention.description: Manufacturing using parameter set PBF-LB/M B (low laser power/low scan speed) derived from previous work on in-situ alloy formation strategies.

parameters.laser_type: redPower QUBE single mode fiber laser
parameters.parameter_set: PBF-LB/M B (low laser power/low scan speed)

structure.description: PBF-LB/M samples with high relative densities

evidence_units.mechanism: The parameter set is assumed to support dissolution of W in the meltpool based on previous work on in-situ alloy formation strategies with high melting particles.

outcome.measurement_method: optical light microscopy and image analysis

evidence_spans: The low laser power/low scan speed parameter set PBF-LB/M B was furthermore derived from previous work on in-situ alloy formation strategies with high melting particles and is assumed to support dissolution of W in the meltpool [ [32] ].
Both parameter sets were selected for this work because they allow manufacturing of PBF-LB/M samples with high relative densities over 99.5%
limitations: The assumption regarding W dissolution is based on previous work and not explicitly proven in the current section's data.

intervention.description: Selection of spherical W-powder with D90 of 23.1 µm to facilitate PBF-LB/M.

evidence_units.mechanism: Spherical powder particles are in general superior to irregular shaped particles with respect to flowability and are consequently preferable for recoatability.
evidence_spans: Spherical powder particles are in general superior to irregular shaped particles with respect to flowability and are consequently preferable.
All powder particles except the V-powder are predominantly spherical and show a good flowability.

intervention.description: Use of milled V-powder because spherical V-powder could not be obtained.

evidence_units.mechanism: The irregular shape of milled V-powder results in lower flowability compared to spherical powder.
evidence_spans: Spherical V-powder could unfortunately not be obtained. Hence, milled V-powder from NMD New Materials Development GmbH (Heemsen, Germany) was used.
The irregular shaped, milled V-powder has a lower flowability than spherical powder.

material.name: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy

intervention.description: Processing using parameter set PBF-LB/M B with high volumetric energy density

structure.description: Sample contains less undissolved particles compared to PBF-LB/M A

evidence_units.mechanism: Higher volumetric energy input, slower scan speeds, longer interaction time with the laser beam, and more favorable powder movement support the dissolution of high melting elements at in-situ alloy formation by PBF-LB/M.

comparison.baseline_material: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy
comparison.baseline_state: built with parameter set PBF-LB/M A
comparison.baseline_value: contains undissolved powder particles identified as tungsten particles

evidence_spans: Parameter set PBF-LB/M B comprises a considerably lower scan speed (100 mm/s vs. 800 mm/s) but, despite the lower laser power, a higher volumetric energy density (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) than parameter set PBF-LB/M A. This facilitates the dissolution of the high melting W particles, thus leading to less undissolved particles as shown in Figure 2 .

material.name: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy

intervention.description: Processing using parameter set PBF-LB/M B with smaller hatch distance and higher volumetric energy density

structure.description: Sample contains wider cracks compared to PBF-LB/M A

evidence_units.mechanism: Smaller hatch distance and higher volumetric energy density cause higher stress values according to the temperature gradient mechanism model that describes the formation of internal stress during PBF-LB/M, leading to cracking of the samples during processing due to brittle grain boundaries and internal stress.

comparison.baseline_material: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy
comparison.baseline_state: built with parameter set PBF-LB/M A

evidence_spans: The different crack patterns in dependence of the parameter set PBF-LB/M A and PBF-LB/M B with wider cracks in the PBF-LB/M B samples are a result of the smaller hatch distance (45 µm vs. 120 µm) and the higher volumetric energy density applied (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) compared to parameter set PBF-LB/M A. According to the temperature gradient mechanism model that describes the formation of internal stress during PBF-LB/M [ [47] , [48] ] both factors together are assumed to cause higher stress values and consequently wider cracks.

material.name: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy

intervention.description: Processing using parameter set PBF-LB/M B resulting in cellular solidification

structure.description: Sample solidifies in an almost cellular structure with only a few secondary dendrites

evidence_units.mechanism: Lower growth rates R and higher temperature gradients in the liquid G favor cellular solidification.

comparison.baseline_material: WMoTaNbV refractory metal high entropy alloy
comparison.baseline_state: built with parameter set PBF-LB/M A (coarser structure)

evidence_spans: Parameter set PBF-LB/M A features a larger structure size and more distinct secondary dendrites, while the material processed with parameter set PBF-LB/M B solidifies in an almost cellular structure with only a few secondary dendrites. These different solidification modes also affect the material properties. The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample with the coarser structure is 561 ± 17 HV0.1 (n = 9) while the microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is 614 ± 21 HV0.1 (n = 9).
